target_customer: People with irritable bowel syndrome who follow or want to avoid the low FODMAP diet (consumers, sold online and through retail partners)
problem: About 18 million Americans have IBS and the standard approach is a restrictive low FODMAP diet. Kiwi Bio sells FODZYME, a tasteless enzyme powder added to food that breaks down FODMAP triggers.
business_model: Direct to consumer consumable (enzyme powder bottles and stick packs) plus retail partners

founders.name: Anjie Liu
education: Harvard University, 2017, joint concentration in physics and comparative literature
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says she has IBS, was diagnosed six years before the article and tried the low FODMAP diet for nearly three years.

founders.name: David Hachuel Gurska
education: Harvard School of Public Health, MPH in epidemiology
Cornell University, Master's in computer and information science
previous_startups: auggi.ai (co-founder and CEO, digital gut health coach for IBS, acquired by Seed Health)

technical_complexity.rationale: Required engineering a novel enzyme blend (fructan hydrolase plus lactase and alpha-galactosidase) that works in food and gut conditions, plus formulation, certification and lab validation.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending fructan hydrolase and Monash low FODMAP certification help, but supplement categories are easy for rivals to enter with similar enzyme blends.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Broad digestive enzyme brands sold single-enzyme products. No acquisition or copycat from them was found in sources opened; later FODMAP enzyme rivals (Fodmate from Casa de Sante, Intoleran) appeared in vendor comparison pages.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported a founder with IBS who tried the restrictive diet for nearly three years. The company cites about 15 percent of the world and 18 million Americans with IBS, and FODZYME launched in May 2021 at 39 dollars a bottle.

branding.domain_note: Product site is fodzyme.com; the company name Kiwi Biosciences (short form Kiwi Bio) differs from the product brand.

identity.logo: FODZYME wordmark with Monash low FODMAP certification mark on site
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and reassuring, tagline Meals Made Painless

branding.brand_signature: Meals Made Painless tagline and the tasteless add-to-any-food powder
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by FODMAP Everyday interviews and stories, Product Hunt launch in July 2021, Telegraph mention for a 2023 UK pharma award finalist listing. No merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: FODZYME combines FODMAP and enzyme, which tells IBS patients what it does, and community outlets repeated it. The parent name Kiwi Biosciences is less known. No evidence of mass awareness. The product name origin is not stated by a source.

outcome_analysis: Kiwi Bio launched FODZYME in May 2021 and raised a 1.5 million dollar seed after the Summer 2021 YC batch, led by a founder with first-hand IBS experience and a second founder who had already built and sold a gut health app. The product won Monash certification and clinical interest, expanded to Australia, the UK and Europe by 2022, and was still updating its formula in 2025. No later round or exit was found, so growth beyond the seed is not publicly documented.
notes: Seed amount of 1.5M comes from TechCrunch, with Seedtable and other aggregators agreeing on 1.5M in October 2021; some trackers show 2M or 1.63M total over 4 rounds, unverified. Aggregators also list Plug and Play and Sequoia, unverified and not recorded. Competitor list is empty: the YC page, company site, TechCrunch and the 2022 press release name no rivals, and the rival comparisons found (Beano, Fodmate, Intoleran) came from undated vendor pages. Beano and Lactaid are noted in takeover_risk as long standing broad enzyme brands, not as dated competitor sources.
